stem: On complete combustion, \(0.246\,\text{g}\) of an organic compound gave \(0.198\,\text{g}\) of carbon dioxide and \(0.1014\,\text{g}\) of water. Determine the percentage composition of carbon and hydrogen in the compound.
solution:
Percentage of carbon \(= \dfrac{12 \times 0.198 \times 100}{44 \times 0.246} = 21.95\%\)

Percentage of hydrogen \(= \dfrac{2 \times 0.1014 \times 100}{18 \times 0.246} = 4.58\%\)

stem: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen, \(0.3\,\text{g}\) of an organic compound gave \(50\,\text{mL}\) of nitrogen collected at \(300\,\text{K}\) temperature and \(715\,\text{mm}\) pressure. Calculate the percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound. (Aqueous tension at \(300\,\text{K} = 15\,\text{mm}\))
solution:
Volume of nitrogen collected at \(300\,\text{K}\) and \(715\,\text{mm}\) pressure is \(50\,\text{mL}\).

Actual pressure \(= 715 - 15 = 700\,\text{mm}\)

Volume of nitrogen at STP \(= \dfrac{273 \times 700 \times 50}{300 \times 760} = 41.9\,\text{mL}\)

\(22{,}400\,\text{mL}\) of \(\text{N}_2\) at STP weighs \(28\,\text{g}\).

\(41.9\,\text{mL}\) of nitrogen weighs \(= \dfrac{28 \times 41.9}{22400}\,\text{g}\)

Percentage of nitrogen \(= \dfrac{28 \times 41.9 \times 100}{22400 \times 0.3} = 17.46\%\)

stem: During estimation of nitrogen present in an organic compound by Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia evolved from \(0.5\,\text{g}\) of the compound in Kjeldahl's estimation of nitrogen neutralized \(10\,\text{mL}\) of \(1\,\text{M}\) \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\). Find out the percentage of nitrogen in the compound.
solution:
\(1\,\text{M}\) of \(10\,\text{mL}\) \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 1\,\text{M}\) of \(20\,\text{mL}\) \(\text{NH}_3\)

\(1000\,\text{mL}\) of \(1\,\text{M}\) ammonia contains \(14\,\text{g}\) nitrogen.

\(20\,\text{mL}\) of \(1\,\text{M}\) ammonia contains \(\dfrac{14 \times 20}{1000}\,\text{g}\) nitrogen.

Percentage of nitrogen \(= \dfrac{14 \times 20 \times 100}{1000 \times 0.5} = 56.0\%\)
_note: The stem and the opening of the solution are on page index 32; the solution completes on page index 33.

stem: In Carius method of estimation of halogen, \(0.15\,\text{g}\) of an organic compound gave \(0.12\,\text{g}\) of \(\text{AgBr}\). Find out the percentage of bromine in the compound.
solution:
Molar mass of \(\text{AgBr} = 108 + 80 = 188\,\text{g mol}^{-1}\)

\(188\,\text{g}\) \(\text{AgBr}\) contains \(80\,\text{g}\) bromine.

\(0.12\,\text{g}\) \(\text{AgBr}\) contains \(\dfrac{80 \times 0.12}{188}\,\text{g}\) bromine.

Percentage of bromine \(= \dfrac{80 \times 0.12 \times 100}{188 \times 0.15} = 34.04\%\)

stem: In sulphur estimation, \(0.157\,\text{g}\) of an organic compound gave \(0.4813\,\text{g}\) of barium sulphate. What is the percentage of sulphur in the compound?
solution:
Molecular mass of \(\text{BaSO}_4 = 137 + 32 + 64 = 233\,\text{g}\)

\(233\,\text{g}\) \(\text{BaSO}_4\) contains \(32\,\text{g}\) sulphur.

\(0.4813\,\text{g}\) \(\text{BaSO}_4\) contains \(\dfrac{32 \times 0.4813}{233}\,\text{g}\) sulphur.

Percentage of sulphur \(= \dfrac{32 \times 0.4813 \times 100}{233 \times 0.157} = 42.10\%\)
